To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) subjects deliver less feedback when simultaneously controlling and providing feedback signals to a robot, 2) subjects may also modify how and when they provide feedback, and 3), subjects are not significantly less accurate when simultaneously controlling and delivering feedback signals.

1) subjects provide less feedback signals when simultaneously providing both control and feedback, 2) subjects modify the quality and quantity of their feedback signals when simultaneously delivering control and feedback, and 3), subjects do not significantly degrade the quality of their control signals when simultaneously providing control and feedback.
1) humans provide less feedback when delivering control and feedback signals simultaneously, and 2) control signal quality is similar in the two cases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of human-robot interfaces that enable human users to simultaneously deliver both control signals and feedback signals to semi-autonomous robots.
the design and evaluation of a general interactive learning paradigm for online cooperation between human and reinforcement learning agents on difficult tasks.
understanding the human factors of human-robot interaction in reinforcement learning domains, and how to better inform the design and development of human-robot collaborative systems.

the simultaneous delivery of feedback and control signals does not significantly impact the quality of the human control signal.
the human control and feedback signals are delivered in different ways and at different times, depending upon whether the signals are provided concurrently or in a sequential fashion.
the human subjects in this study are able to provide simultaneous control and feedback, and that the quality of control signals is not diminished when the subjects provide feedback at the same time.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are able to train an RL agent to perform a complex task in a simulated domain, with the help of human feedback and control, in a way that is both efficient and effective.
the human control signal was not significantly affected by simultaneous delivery of reward-shaping feedback.
the human control signal quality is maintained when providing simultaneous control and feedback and that the human feedback signal quality is reduced.

the human control and feedback signals are not independent.
